newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt to privatise Telia - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt to privatise Telia - newspaper.

text.p: The Swedish government will next month propose privatising national telephone operator Telia, a daily newspaper reported on Tuesday.
"The reason for the privatisation is said to be that Telia needs five billion crowns in capital injection during the next few years," political daily Dagens Politik said.
Telia needs the money mainly to meet increased competition when the EU's telecommunications market is fully deregulated in 1998, but also to meet current domestic competition, the newspaper said.
The listing is expected, at the earliest, late in the autumn of 1997, the newspaper said. The government will keep a majority stake in the phone operator, it added.

Brokerage Carnegie estimates Telia's market capitalisation has fallen to about 45 billion crowns from 66 billion crowns two years ago as investors have plenty of European telecoms shares to choose from following a slew of privatisations.
The supply will become even larger as more privatisations are presented, putting further pressure on the government to decide about a privatisation of Telia.
